summary: SunriseHealth production: KV prefix corruption triggered dedicated pool failover loop and streaming disconnects
description:
Issue summary:
SunriseHealth reported widespread streaming disconnects, truncated completions, and intermittent 5xx errors starting 2026-03-10 02:43 UTC. Customer traffic on a dedicated GPU pool entered a failover loop where requests were continuously retried across model variants and regions, causing high tail latency and duplicated token billing.

Impact:
- ~48% of SunriseHealth requests in us-east experienced streaming resets or 5xx between 02:43–04:10 UTC.
- Customer reported degraded user experience for real-time triage workflows and a billing spike due to request retries.
- Affects dedicated tier; customer-facing SLAs at risk.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool: dp-us-east-03
- Serving runtime version: 1.28.3 (post-kernel-rollout)
- Smart routing policy: latency-prefer, fallback allowed to quantized variants
- KV cache configuration: prefix-based KV caching enabled with LRU eviction

Steps to reproduce (summary):
1) Send streaming chat requests pinned to gpt-large-v2-quantized with long context (>2k tokens).
2) Observe intermittent streaming disconnects and then rapid retries to fallback model.
3) After retries, duplicate tokens appear in billing logs and clients receive out-of-order tokens.

Key logs & traces:
- Gateway logs show repeated 502/504 with "kv-prefix-inconsistency" traces.
- Serving runtime trace: inconsistent KV lookup returned null for existing prefixes, triggering fallback and reinitialization of KV client.
- Autoscaler logs: brief scale-in events correlated with kernel-selection health-check flapping.
investigation_notes:
Timeline & findings:
- 02:40 UTC: kernel-selection rollout (1.28.3) completed for dp-us-east-03. Change included an optimization that rehashes KV prefix keys when selecting quantized execution path.
- 02:43 UTC: First customer report. Initial hypothesis: regression in new kernel-selection path causing miss-keying of prefix keys.
- 02:55 UTC: Observed repeated cache miss + reinitialize behavior on serving nodes; KV client returned corrupted prefix checksum for a subset of prefixes.
- 03:10 UTC: Correlation found between nodes that had upgraded to 1.28.3 and those emitting "kv-prefix-inconsistency". Nodes running 1.28.2 were stable.
- 03:22 UTC: Root cause: a race in the prefix-rehash code path where concurrent writes during rehash could leave a prefix in a partially-updated state. This manifested under long-context streaming workloads (large KV entries) and triggered failover logic in smart-routing.
- Additional observation: when smart-routing fallback engaged, requests were retried to quantized variants which caused duplicate token accounting because request deduplication relied on stable KV prefix IDs.

Hypotheses tested:
- Rolling back kernel-selection patch on a single node reduced instances of prefix inconsistency for traffic routed to that node (confirmed).
- Purging KV cache on affected nodes temporarily restored normal behavior but did not address underlying race (temporary mitigation only).

Telemetry & data collected:
- Exported traces to S3: s3://redwood-ops/sup-999101/traces/2026-03-10/
- Billing delta snapshot exported for SunriseHealth for 02:00–05:00 UTC.
resolution:
Mitigation steps completed by 03:55 UTC on 2026-03-10:
1) Immediately rolled back serving-runtime to 1.28.2 for dp-us-east-03 and prevented further rollout.
2) Cleared KV caches on all affected nodes (orchestrated cache flush).
3) Temporarily tightened smart-routing to disable automatic fallback to quantized variants for SunriseHealth traffic.
4) Deployed hotfix PR (https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4821) that adds a mutex around prefix rehash and protective checksum validation; promoted to canary and then to dp-us-east-03 by 2026-03-11 09:12 UTC.

Outcome:
- Streaming stability restored and 5xx rates returned to baseline within ~30 minutes of rollback/flush.
- Hotfix validated in staging and deployed to affected dedicated pool. No further occurrences reported after deployment.

Customer communication:
- Notified SunriseHealth SRE and CSM at 03:15 UTC with incident status and immediate mitigations.
- Provided post-incident summary and billing reconciliation promise; finance review initiated for overcharge.
- Customer accepted workaround and requested postmortem and preventive actions.
follow_up_actions: Complete detailed postmortem and share with customer by 2026-03-12
Add integration test that simulates concurrent prefix-rehash under long-context streaming
Improve canary gating to include KV-integrity checks before kernel-selection rollout
Backfill billing reconciliation for duplicated tokens and issue credit if confirmed
Add dashboard alert for kv-prefix-inconsistency traces and increase telemetry retention for dedicated pools
